title: Option::unwrap() in non-test code on socket path (2 sites)
description:
rust.md: "Never use `Option::unwrap()`. When `None` would indicate a bug, use `.expect(\"reason the value should be Some\")`."

- persona/src/main.rs:76 — `let path_str = path.to_str().unwrap().to_owned();`
- persona-nmh/src/main.rs:118 — `let path = socket_path().to_str().unwrap().to_owned();`

Both unwrap `Path::to_str()`, which is `None` for non-UTF-8 paths. The path is `/run/user/{uid}/persona/workload.sock` built from `libc::getuid()`, so it is always ASCII and `None` is genuinely unreachable — which is exactly the case rust.md says to write as `.expect()` with the invariant stated. Today the failure surfaces as a bare `called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value` with no indication of what was being unwrapped.

Fix: `.expect("socket path is built from a uid and is always valid UTF-8")` at both sites.
close_reason: Fixed in da71bf3, but NOT as the bead directed. The bead prescribed .expect("socket path is built from a uid and is always valid UTF-8"). That invariant is stale: since the socket path moved behind workload_socket_path() it derives from $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (or Darwin confstr), which is arbitrary bytes, not uid-built ASCII. An .expect() there would have enshrined a false claim and still panicked. Both call sites instead drop the conversion entirely -- UnixStream::connect takes AsRef<Path>, so the String was never needed. Removes the panic, the allocation, and the UTF-8 requirement. Line numbers were also stale (persona/src/main.rs:35 not :76; persona-nmh/src/main.rs:115 not :118). Verified: cargo clippy clean, full workspace tests pass, commit builds standalone.
